I think the toughest part about balancing is addressing the differences between casual matches and professional play. There are many characters that dominate in lower skill levels but aren't utilized in competitive settings. You might wonder why not just balance for professional play only? Well, then the majority of the player base would be left with a hero pool that has extreme win rates, which can drop to the 30% range because they are too strong in professional play, and players generally dislike that. 

This game has a few characters that have really low win rates but are extensively used in professional play, yet I would say the number of characters in this category is fairly low, so it doesn't disrupt casual matches much. The fine line in balance is being able to cater to both professional and casual play, such as when they made a character easier to play for the average player but harder for professionals, which is a step in the right direction.

Now, what about the characters that dominate in casual play but struggle in competitive settings? Any time a character reaches a 55% win rate, it becomes permanently banned and heavily criticized. This is also quite challenging; you can make the character harder to play, but more importantly, ensure their abilities aren't overly oppressive. There are two characters with around a 60% win rate in casual play, both of which aren't played much in competitive settings nor have a high pick rate in casual matches, due to the nature of their abilities (they are healing-type characters, but not as oppressive as others).

It looks like a pretty good card actually, but there are a few nuances.  

-First, life total is 20 in the card game, so you don't heal as much.  
-Huge thing, the card is sorcery speed which means you can only play it on your own turn, which is a big deal in the card game because it means you invest your resources upfront.  
-You already know that certain cards don't automatically turn a lost game into a won game. How many times do you heal to full but get defeated by an aggressive deck with a powerful creature and one more weapon? The same applies here; if you don't have board presence, you're destroyed anyway.  
-All resources spent this turn being overloaded is NOT a drawback to take lightly. Spending 3 resources means you're minimum overloaded for 3, which costs you 6 resources over 2 turns at the very least, but if you want to play this card with something else, then you're overloaded for even more.  
-Lastly, it can be a dead draw early on. A simple 3 resource heal for 8 is at least castable early on if you have nothing else to do, even if you heal less than 8, but you can't play this because the drawback messes up your next turn, so you only play it for its full value.  

Edit: It's an interesting design and I like the card. The card game has a lot of "emergency" cards where you get a huge deal upfront but pay an extreme cost later. They have several cards that do "something insane" followed by "you lose the game next turn."
